serviceCards.title: Individual Therapy
serviceCards.tagline: Understand yourself. Find a way forward.
serviceCards.description: For people navigating anxiety, low mood, grief, trauma, stress, self-worth concerns and difficult life transitions.

serviceCards.title: Couples Therapy
serviceCards.tagline: For two people who still want to understand what is happening between them.
serviceCards.description: A structured, balanced space to explore recurring patterns, improve communication, address conflict and work towards a healthier relationship.

serviceCards.title: Before You Marry
serviceCards.tagline: Prepare for the marriage, not just the wedding.
serviceCards.description: A five-session premarital counselling programme exploring money, family expectations, faith, values, communication, intimacy and how to navigate disagreements.

serviceCards.title: The Annual Review
serviceCards.tagline: A yearly check-in for your marriage.
serviceCards.description: You do not have to wait until your marriage is in trouble before giving it attention.

serviceCards.title: The Intensive
serviceCards.tagline: Focused therapeutic work, with more time to explore.
serviceCards.description: An opportunity to work on a specific concern over one or two full days, with time for focused exploration, reflection and planning.

serviceCards.title: Diaspora Sessions
serviceCards.description: Online therapeutic support for Nigerians living outside the country, with someone who understands the cultural context they may be navigating.

beliefs.title: The relationship you have with yourself matters.
beliefs.body: How you understand yourself, manage your emotions and respond to difficult experiences can influence the relationships you build. That is why I often begin with the individual, even when the concern is about a marriage.

beliefs.title: Conflict is not the end. What happens next matters.
beliefs.body: Disagreements are part of relationships. What matters is how we respond to them, whether we take responsibility for our actions, and whether we can repair the hurt. Learning to reconnect after conflict is a skill that can be developed.

beliefs.title: Counselling is not a courtroom.
beliefs.body: I am not here to declare a winner or decide which partner is entirely right. My role is to help you understand what is happening, recognise the patterns contributing to the problem and explore a healthier way forward. I will be honest with you, even when the conversation is uncomfortable.

beliefs.title: A healthy relationship is built, not discovered.
beliefs.body: Compatibility matters, but a lasting relationship also requires self-awareness, communication, emotional responsibility and a willingness to grow. Finding someone you love is one thing. Learning how to build a healthy relationship together is another.

processSteps.title: The introductory call
processSteps.body: We begin with a brief, 15-minute conversation. You explain what brings you here, ask initial questions and explore whether my services are a suitable fit. This is an introductory conversation, not a therapy session or assessment.

processSteps.title: Understanding your concerns
processSteps.body: Your first paid session gives us time to explore your experiences, current challenges and what you hope to achieve. Together, we identify the concerns you want to address and begin establishing meaningful goals for our work.

processSteps.title: Doing the work
processSteps.body: We work towards your agreed goals, exploring patterns, developing insight and practising new ways of responding to difficulties. The process will depend on your circumstances, the service you choose and the progress we make together.

processSteps.title: Reviewing your progress
processSteps.body: We pause to consider what has changed, what still needs attention and whether to continue, adjust our approach or conclude the work. Reviews take place at appropriate points based on the service and your individual needs.
